sources.authority: Bloomberg News, republished by Bloomberg Law
sources.passage: It reports that, at a company-wide meeting that week, Altman said OpenAI could potentially pace development with several other labs; people familiar with the private details requested anonymity. It says some labs may not agree.
sources.limitation: This is attributed reporting of an internal discussion. It does not establish an announced pause, a pact, a timeline, or a product-policy change. The accessible reprint locks the remainder of the article.

sources.passage: Reuters reports Bloomberg said Altman told staff OpenAI was open to slowing development amid safety concerns and might pace development with other labs. Reuters says an Anthropic spokesperson expressed interest in working with the industry on the pace of releasing new tools.
sources.limitation: Reuters is relaying the Bloomberg report, rather than documenting an independent eyewitness account of the staff meeting. The Anthropic spokesperson statement is interest, not an agreement or an announced joint action.

sources.passage: Pachocki writes that OpenAI will seek to align, monitor, and build defenses against more powerful systems and will unilaterally withhold further scaling as needed; he says broader interventions will also be needed.
sources.limitation: This official post predates the report and does not confirm that Altman made the reported staff-meeting remarks, that OpenAI has slowed development, or that other labs agreed to do so.

claimBoundaries: Describe the staff-meeting account as Bloomberg reporting based on unnamed people familiar with a private meeting.
Do not say OpenAI has slowed development, that any laboratory agreed, that a timetable exists, or that ChatGPT changed.
Treat the Anthropic spokesperson response as interest, not an agreement.
Treat Pachocki’s September 6 post as separate context, not confirmation of the reported meeting.
